mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within the last 2 months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment are expected to increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% within the last 2 months, it signals a weakening demand with inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer purchasing power and confidence are expected to decline.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 3% signals rising inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% and real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% within the last quarter, it signals a strong supply-side growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% and GDPC1 increases > 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
